notes: SHIP v1.14.366 - OPS WALL CELL ART, BOTH SHELLS. The nine BUILD wall cells now carry their tool raster as a background layer behind the existing content. Owner ruling: art goes BEHIND content, cell layout and every text child stay structurally byte-identical, no growth, no line replacement, no reflow - and the ship must land correctly in BOTH shells, tuned per shell rather than one inheriting the other's values. MECHANISM, chosen for least change: a per-cell --tim custom property feeding a three-layer background on the EXISTING .opswall cell rule. No new elements, no positioned img, no z-index, no markup restructure - the only markup change is --tim appended inside each cell's existing style attribute. Background layers always paint behind a box's own content, so all four text children sit above the veil automatically. LAYER ORDER, top to bottom: the veil, then the art, then the ORIGINAL .359 accent tint retained as the base. Keeping that tint underneath is deliberate rather than vestigial: a cell whose image fails to load renders exactly as it did in .365 instead of dropping to flat black, which is the same standing 'a missing asset must not look deliberate' mechanism the banner rows use. STEP 0 FINDING - THE WALL IS ONE SHARED MARKUP BLOCK, NOT DUPLICATED. Verified: one .opswall, one #wk-opswall, one #wk-opsrow, one render path. The half-ship failure mode the owner was guarding against - wiring landing in the desk block and silently missing the phone - cannot occur here, because there is no second block. Shells are switched by CSS media query ONLY: no body class, no separate render path, no asset-shell machinery (the file's single <picture> and single srcset are both inside a comment recording that no such mechanism exists). Breakpoints act on #work-grid max-width: base = full width, 640px = 760px, 980px = 1080px. ART FIT IS PER-SHELL, AND THIS CORRECTED THE SPEC'S PREMISE. The spec anticipated that 256 sources would merely soft-scale on desk and asked whether 512 masters were warranted. Measurement showed the real problem is aspect crop, which is resolution-independent: at a 1280px viewport a cell renders 348x88, an aspect of 3.95:1, while every source raster is 1:1. Under cover that fills the width and then discards 75% of the icon's height, leaving a soft band through its middle - and a 512 master would only have made that band sharper. Owner ruled contain on desk. Phone keeps cover: at 107x88 it still shows 82% of the icon and filling the cell reads better there. Desk takes contain: an 88x88 icon centred in a 348px cell, DOWNSCALED from 256 and therefore sharp, with the accent tint showing around it. Net effect is that the existing 256 masters are now correct on both shells rather than merely adequate, and NO new art cut is needed. VEIL ALPHAS ARE SHELL-SCOPED KNOBS: --veil-t/--veil-b are declared once for phone and again in the 640px block, both starting at .55 top and .85 bottom by ruling. The duplicate declaration is the point - raising or lowering one shell can never silently move the other. They are expected to part company after the two-device verify, and the standing rule is that text legibility wins over art visibility in every cell, both shells, no exceptions. FILE MAPPING IS EXACTLY AS RULED and no file was renamed: bom, manifest, portmap, rackmap, sops, burndown and audits take their phantom-tool-*-256 raster; BLAST takes phantom-tool-power-256 (it has never existed as phantom-tool-blastradius-256, which was a name in the request that no file on disk has ever carried); OPTICS takes phantom-ref-optics-256. All nine were verified present on disk before wiring. NO NEW PRECACHE ENTRIES: all nine rasters were already in PRECACHE_URLS, so this ship adds zero bytes to a cold install and carries none of the usual asset-ship offline risk. sw.js changes by the cache version alone. DEPLOY_TOOLS LEFT UNTOUCHED as ruled - its dormant img field is a separate cleanup. Worth recording that until this ship those eight rasters rendered on NO surface at all: their only reference was that dead field, which nothing reads (meta.name is the sole property any consumer touches). They shipped and precached and painted nowhere; the wall is now their first real consumer. GATES: three-stamp lockstep; all four inline JS blocks + sw.js compile; 12 style blocks brace-balanced; ops-cell still exactly 9 (owner's standing acceptance check); all nine rd_openOpsTool handlers byte-unchanged; every text child byte-identical; exactly 3 files touched. DEVICE-VERIFY IS TWO-DEVICE: (1) badge reads v1.14.366. (2) iPhone at 390px: nine cells show art filling the cell behind the labels; every label legible. (3) Laptop shell: nine cells show the WHOLE icon centred and sharp, not a cropped band. (4) ALL NINE CELLS MUST STILL TAP THROUGH in both shells - art must never cost a door. (5) Cell height unchanged in both shells; the wall must not have grown or reflowed. (6) If any label is marginal over art, the lever is that shell's --veil-b, and only that shell's. (7) ?legacy=1 unchanged - #work-grid is display:none outside body.rd. ROLLBACK: revert this commit - cells return to flat accent tint with every door and every readout intact.
